title: Money String
statement: Implement `solve(raw)`. `raw` is a string the caller claims is a money amount. If it is not a string, return `error`. This includes the case where you would have received a JSON number. The tests pass either a string or the token `float`. Accept a string of digits with an optional decimal point and exactly two decimal places when a point is present, or digits only. Return the normalized two-decimal string using Decimal. Reject a leading sign, spaces, and anything else with `error`.
constraints: The token float means the input was a binary float and is rejected
hints: If raw is the string float, return error immediately.
Parse other strings with Decimal only when the text matches digits and an optional .dd.
Quantize to two places and return str.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A JSON number is a binary float by the time many stacks hand it to you, and money cannot round-trip through that.

editorial: A JSON number is a binary float by the time many stacks hand it to you, and money cannot round-trip through that. Requiring a string keeps the exact digits. The pattern check rejects signs and extra dots before Decimal sees them.
